state.request: The user asks whether introducing first-class fragment declarations and render references is better or worse for AI coding agents, and explicitly requests JEV consultation. Evaluate adoption through source token economy and reliable agent generation/editing. There is no implemented compiler/runtime or measured agent benchmark. This is advisory design judgment, not proof of performance.
state.existing_design: Then declares pages and supported PatternFly components. Runtime automatically derives render regions and HTMX fragment responses for forms/actions. Ordinary navigation returns a full page. No source hx-* attributes or separate rendering implementation. Existing reference apps do not show repeated component subtrees across different pages. Rendering always rechecks current record/field policy and team context.

candidate_examples.automatic:
Then
  page / title="Tasks"
    list Todo
      edit
      delete
candidate_examples.extracted:
Then
  fragment tasks
    list Todo
      edit

candidate_examples.inline_name:
Then

      edit
      delete

tradeoffs: Automatic regions keep one-use code local and shortest. Agents do not choose names/targets but generated boundaries must have a documented stable runtime contract. Reusing the same subtree on multiple pages repeats source unless a reuse form exists.

Extracted fragments provide a stable reusable symbol and a single update location when multiple pages genuinely share the same subtree. They add declarations, render references and potentially explicit typed parameters; agents may over-extract one-use content or introduce name/scope errors.
Inline id naming provides an explicit boundary/target without moving code elsewhere. It adds an attribute and uniqueness/scope rules but does not deduplicate cross-page markup.

No new primitive may bypass authorization or generate a separate business operation. Source fragment/render/id syntax is only a proposal, not currently part of the chosen design. Public standalone fragment routes are not required just to support generated HTMX interactions.

A reusable parameterized fragment cannot infer a parent record from whichever page most recently rendered it; its record bindings must be explicit, typed and checked. Common team/auth context should remain shared.

The user strongly opposes unnecessary layers and repeated tokens. Token cost should be considered over both initial generation and later edits; number of files/keywords alone does not measure reliability.

single_use.instructions: For a one-page app whose task list is rendered in exactly one place, choose the most justified source form for AI generation and later ordinary edits.

criteria.automatic: Keep components inline and let runtime generate partial boundaries/targets. No extra source symbol; rely on a documented runtime region contract.
criteria.extracted: Declare the named fragment separately and render it once, paying naming/reference tokens for explicit reuse identity and location.
criteria.inline_name: Keep the component inline with an explicit id attribute, paying naming tokens for target identity without extraction.
criteria.unresolved: The given evidence does not justify choosing one form.

actual_reuse.instructions: For an identical substantial subtree rendered by three pages and frequently changed together, choose the most justified form, assuming reusable-fragment inputs are explicit and typed.

criteria.repeat_inline: Repeat each page's subtree, preserving local context and eliminating render references at the cost of repeated tokens and coordinated edits.
criteria.shared_fragment: Define one named reusable fragment and render it from each page with typed bindings, reducing repetition at the cost of names/parameters and navigation.
criteria.inline_name: Name each inline subtree but retain separate copies, providing target identity and local context without cross-page deduplication.
criteria.unresolved: The given evidence does not justify choosing one form.

v1_policy.instructions: Choose a v1 policy for this repository given its current reference apps, user priorities and lack of empirical agent measurements.

criteria.automatic_only_now: Keep automatic inline regions in v1; defer reusable fragments until a concrete app demonstrates repeated content worth extracting. Current syntax stays smaller; future repetition might require an extension.
criteria.optional_reuse_now: Add fragment/render now as optional typed reuse, retaining automatic inline defaults. Covers later repeated UI but introduces scope/name rules before a current app demonstrates the need.
criteria.mandatory_fragments_now: Require named fragment/render for updateable regions, making boundaries explicit uniformly at the cost of more declarations/references in simple apps.
criteria.optional_inline_names_now: Add optional inline id naming now, retain automatic defaults, and defer reusable-fragment extraction. Addresses explicit targeting but not source deduplication.
criteria.unresolved: Evidence is insufficient; defer this decision pending a targeted agent benchmark.
